name: apis-ax-axp
description: The apis.ax curation gate as an api.qa PinnedSpec: the machine-checkable form of AXP, the Agent eXperience Protocol. Every RFC-2119 MUST clause is pinned to its OWN discriminating verification — a specific api.qa check (kind:'check') or a behavioral probe — so no clause rides a coarse aggregate that would tolerate its violation. Every requirement restates an obligation printed in PROTOCOL.md; the eight probe requirements are verbatim its Appendix A.4, resolved against the target's own card-declared probe manifest (agents.json `probes`, Appendix A.3) and failing closed when it is absent, incomplete, or invalid. The manifest declares only WHERE the verifier probes; what counts as passing lives here, and the verifier derives the over-ceiling, below-ceiling, and zero amounts itself. The knownEmpty/knownForbidden pathnames must also be observed serving 200 OK in the same run (pathMustServeOk), so a dedicated decoy endpoint cannot satisfy Clause 4. Clause 3's deterministic content negotiation (three faces, address > Accept > client-class precedence, Link alternates — Appendix A.7) is pinned via the four conneg checks plus machine-legible-home, and conneg-forced-face fails closed when a home advertises no resolvable alternates. api.qa (held outside the building fleet's write access) verifies a target against this contract; a Listing is admitted to the catalog iff api.qa returns passed: true. Two requirements — `check-digital-link-resolver` and `check-published-test-suite` — are DECLARATION-ARMED (PROTOCOL.md Appendix A.8): `appliesWhen: { cardDeclares: 'interfaces.<name>' }` applies each only to a card that declares that optional interface, and a card that omits it passes as not applicable. `check-published-test-suite` holds a declaring card to its own published, digest-pinned suite in the dialect its card names: `api.qa/suite@1` interpreted as declarative data, or `api.qa/vitest@1` executed under the Appendix A.8.6 invariants (fresh single-use isolate, zero ambient authority, a network floor barring metadata/link-local/private/verifier-internal destinations with full external egress above it, a metered circuit-breaker deadline — default 300s wall / 60s CPU, billed to the requesting account: the runner is a PAID-TIER capability, the paid tier (never scarcity) is its gate, and the remaining bounds are abuse circuit-breakers, never rations — 4MiB-output, 1000-combined, 1MiB-document and 4MiB-module caps, executed bytes hash-then-instantiated from the card-pinned buffer, fail-closed on any mismatch). The pinned suite artifact is addressed by the card as one of three collapsed channels (Appendix A.8.6.6): the suite document itself with tests as string members, a natively served ES module at a versioned URL, or an npm package@version coordinate as an identity assertion over the served bytes — in every addressing the digest is the sole authority, and a registry is never in the loop. A third requirement — `check-capability-coverage` (PROTOCOL.md Appendix A.8.7) — is DECLARATION-ARMED on the same card key, `interfaces.testSuite`: one declaration, two strictly judged facets, which A.8 permits because the registry is keyed by check, never by card key. Over the SAME single suite run (one run, two judgments, never a second execution), every capability the card declares MUST be covered by at least one PASSING row or test: every contract operation (`openapi:<operationId>`, or `openapi:<METHOD> <path>` when no operationId exists), every `interfaces.http` entry resolved to its contract operation (the unconditionally verified faces /.well-known/agents.json, /openapi.json and /llms.txt exempt), every declared MCP tool (`mcp:<toolName>`, or `interfaces.mcp` when no tools array is declared), and every other optional declared interface (`interfaces.<name>`, testSuite itself excluded — the suite is the instrument of proof). Tests bind to identifiers by the pinned artifact's own explicit `coverage` map (root member or module export: identifier -> row ids / full folded test names) unioned with implicit square-bracket coverage tags in row ids and test names; a coverage key, tag, or reference naming anything outside the domain fails (presence-when-true applies to coverage claims), an uncovered identifier fails, and a card that omits `interfaces.testSuite` passes the requirement as not applicable — declared-but-untested is inadmissible, undeclared is untouched. That armed form is additive only: it is legal solely on a `kind: 'check'` requirement whose check this standard registers in the A.8 `axp:optional-interfaces` block against exactly that card key, and never on a check any of Clauses 1-7 binds — so no MUST of this spec is escapable by omitting a card key, and a verifier refuses a spec that tries rather than returning a lenient verdict. Since apis-ax-axp@2.6.0 (AXP 0.9.0) the CHECK `offers-402` is itself conditional on the OBSERVED pricing model, mirroring the appliesWhen gate its pinned requirement has carried since 2.1.0: against a surface whose observed Pricing Document (probes.pricing entry 0, Appendix A.2) declares model:'free' and whose card declares NO purchasable surface — no monetization.offers, no monetization.probe — the check passes VACUOUSLY, because a free property has no 402 boundary to prove and the no-ask zone is satisfied trivially. The rule is fail-closed on both edges: only the observed 'free' declaration earns the vacuous pass (an unobserved, non-JSON, or undetermined model keeps the hard fail), and anything a card DOES declare is judged strictly — a free card declaring either monetization member made a claim and is held to it (Appendix A.8's defective-declaration rule), and the metered half of Clause 5 is unweakened: a metered surface must still declare monetization.offers, hard ceilings, and the behaviorally probed 402 OFFER boundary. No requirement row moves in this ratification; the version and digest move because the check semantics this contract binds to are part of the contract.
